n: In this lesson we will consider the forensic medical examination of living persons from the standpoint of sexual conditions and sexual offences. The forensic medical examination of living persons is the type of examination most often carried out in practice. It is ordered in criminal, civil and administrative cases. In sexual conditions, sex, virginity, maturity, reproductive capacity, pregnancy, childbirth, abortion, sexually transmitted diseases and HIV infection are determined. Sexual offences include rape, sodomy and indecent acts; infection with sexually transmitted diseases or HIV is also studied in this group. Outline of the lesson: 12.3 sexual conditions, 12.4 sexual offences, and 12.5 the procedure for conducting the examination of living persons.

t: Examination of living persons: when it is ordered
n: We shall see when the examination of living persons is ordered. Examinations of living persons are among those most often carried out in practice. They are ordered in various circumstances in criminal, civil and administrative cases. The examination is carried out in the departments of forensic medical institutions, and in some cases also in treatment facilities. The types of examination include bodily injuries, sexual conditions, sexual offences, and state of health and age. In sexual conditions, sex, virginity, maturity and pregnancy are determined, while in sexual offences, rape, sodomy and indecent acts are studied.

The general algorithm of the examination consists of several stages. The circumstances of the event are first studied from the data in the decision or ruling ordering the examination. Then the originals of the medical documents are studied, the person is interviewed about the event and complaints, and then an examination is carried out with the aid of instruments. If necessary, a laboratory examination or consultation is added, and the final document is the expert's conclusion. The originals of the medical documents must be provided; the person is identified by a document such as a passport. In sexual conditions and offences, in addition to the document, two photographs of the person are provided.

We shall dwell on documents and confirmation of identity. The originals of the medical documents must be provided, and the person who ordered the examination is responsible for their reliability. Studying the documents before the examination determines what to pay attention to at the interview and examination. This is especially important in determining the initial state of an injury. Identity is confirmed by a passport, military ID or birth certificate. In exceptional cases it may be certified by the person who ordered the examination. In the examination of sexual conditions and offences, in addition to the identity document, two photographs of the person examined are also provided.

Rules for conducting the examination. The person who ordered the examination may be present at it. Only when a person of the other sex is examined undressed does the investigator or inquiry officer leave the room. Minors are examined in the presence of parents or teachers. Persons lacking legal capacity are examined in the presence of a legal representative. Injuries and other circumstances found at the examination may be photographed only with the person's permission. The examination of a patient undergoing treatment is carried out only if his state of health permits. Information about the examination is entered in the case history.

Quick question: algorithm and rules. First question: list in order the 6 stages of the general algorithm of the examination of living persons. Answer: circumstances of the event, medical documents, interview of the person, examination, additional examination or consultation, expert's conclusion. Second question: when does the investigator leave the examination room? Answer: when a person of the other sex is examined undressed. Third question: what is required in the examination of sexual conditions besides the identity document? Answer: two photographs.

Now the examination of sexual conditions. Examination of sexual conditions is necessary in the investigation of criminal cases and the hearing of civil cases. The following are determined: sex, sexual maturity, virginity and reproductive capacity. In addition, current or past pregnancy, childbirth and abortion are determined. Thus this section includes determination of sex, sexual maturity, virginity, reproductive capacity, and questions of pregnancy, childbirth and abortion.

t: Determination of sex: when it is necessary
n: We shall see when determination of sex is necessary. If sex has been determined incorrectly, or doubt has arisen about the recorded sex, an examination is ordered. Usually the external sexual characteristics form in accordance with the existing gonad, that is, the ovary or testis. Because of defects of the embryonic period, the external genitalia may not fully correspond to the sex. Cases in which the examination is necessary: issuing an identity document, admission to a special educational institution, dissolution of marriage and alimony, and investigation of sexual offences.

Hermaphroditism, true and false types. The presence of sexual organs characteristic of both sexes at the same time is called hermaphroditism; it has true and false types. The true type is very rare; in practice false hermaphroditism is more common. In the true type, male and female glands are present together. In the false male there is a testis and spermatogenesis is observed, but the penis is small and the breast is enlarged. In the false female there is an ovary and oogenesis is observed, but the clitoris is large and the breast is undeveloped. Attention: in the false type, the external features resemble not the sex of the gland but the other sex.

Case analysis: determination of sex. Situation: the external sexual characteristics of the person resemble one sex, while the gonad is characteristic of the other. This may be false hermaphroditism. Attention: in true hermaphroditism there are glands of both sexes, whereas in the false type the gland belongs to one sex. For example, in a false male the testis functions, while the features resemble the female. The examination studies menstruation, nocturnal emissions, history of sexual drive, specialists' documents, anthropometry, external organs and secondary characteristics. Question: if the gland and the characteristics do not correspond, which examination determines the genetic sex? Answer: examination of the chromosomes in blood leukocytes.

The concept of sexual maturity. Sexual maturity is the level of development that allows sexual life without harm to health and further development. In women it means intercourse, becoming pregnant, carrying a pregnancy, giving birth and nursing; in men, the ability to have intercourse and to fertilise. Usually those under 14 years of age are regarded as immature; the question arises in the period from 14 years to the age of marriage. Hereditary, social and geographical factors influence sexual maturation. At present this question is not as important in sexual offences as before, because in the Criminal Code liability is tied to a definite age: Articles 118, 119, 128, 129.

Criteria of maturity in girls. The anthropometric norms are at least as follows: standing height 150 cm, sitting height 80 cm, chest circumference 78–80 cm. Pelvic dimensions: interspinous 26–27 cm, intercristal 29 cm, external conjugate 17–18 cm. The indices are of relative significance: even with smaller dimensions a woman can bear a healthy child. In girls under 14, higher indices may be found because of acceleration. By 16–17 the pelvis allows a normal course of labour; the examination is carried out with the participation of an obstetrician-gynaecologist.

t: Maturity and the age limits in the Criminal Code
n: Let us link maturity and the age limits of the Criminal Code. Up to 14 years a person is usually regarded as sexually immature; the question arises from 14 years to the age of marriage. Formerly maturity was necessary in sexual offences, but now its practical significance is not what it was. The reason: in the Criminal Code liability is set according to a definite age. In Articles 118 and 119 the age limits are 18 and 14, and in Articles 128 and 129 it is 16. The question of maturity arises from the age of 14.

Case analysis: sexual maturity. Situation: in a girl over 14, the question of maturity is raised. The examination is carried out with the participation of an obstetrician-gynaecologist, with clinical and laboratory examinations. After ovulation pregnancy is possible; it is linked with a regular menstrual cycle. At maturity the body of the uterus makes up two thirds, and the cervix one third. In boys the examination is carried out with a urologist or andrologist: general development, external genitalia, secondary characteristics and gonadal function are studied. Question: the pelvic dimensions are somewhat small, but the other signs are sufficient. Is it right to deny maturity on the basis of pelvic dimensions alone?

t: Virginity and structure of the hymen
n: Virginity and structure of the hymen. Virginity, that is virginitas, is determined mainly by the anatomical integrity of the hymen. The hymen is a duplication of the vaginal mucous membrane, containing connective tissue and muscle fibres, vessels and nerves. It lies between the vestibule and the vagina, perpendicular to the axis of the vagina. In the hymen, the base, free edge and opening are distinguished. There may be several openings or none; the shape, height, thickness and density vary. In virginity, when the tip of a finger is carefully inserted into the opening, a constricting ring is felt. In describing the hymen, comparison with a clock face is used.

Forms of the hymen. The classification is given according to M.D. Nikitin and M.G. Serdyukov: the forms of the hymen are divided into three groups. The first group is common and is regarded as usual: annular, semilunar and tubular forms. In the second group the edge is uneven: lobed, spiral and toothed forms, which are called unusual. The third group is very rare: bivalve, septate and cribriform forms. Remember: in the hymen the base, free edge and opening are distinguished, and the form is defined by them. There may be several openings or none; in the description, comparison with a clock face is used.

Defloration, complete and incomplete tear. Violation of the integrity of the hymen at first sexual intercourse, that is defloration, usually leads to loss of virginity. In intercourse, under the action of the glans penis, complete or incomplete tears occur. In a complete tear the injury reaches the base of the hymen, whereas in an incomplete tear it does not reach the base. Integrity may be violated also by other causes: a finger, various objects, a surgical operation. In addition, with an elastic, low hymen or one with many notches, intercourse may take place even without defloration.

t: Dynamics of healing of a tear (timeline)
n: We shall look at the dynamics of healing of a tear along a timeline. At first the edges of the tear bleed for several days, and the area is swollen and covered with blood clots. Then a whitish coating appears. At the end of the 1st week granulation forms and inflammation decreases. From the end of the 2nd week to the 3rd week a scar forms. After 3 weeks the age becomes uncertain: after three weeks it is impossible to determine the age of the violation of integrity, so one should apply sooner.

t: Distinguishing a tear from a natural notch
n: Distinguishing a tear from a natural notch. Sometimes a tear of the hymen must be distinguished from a natural notch. Attention: a tear is not equal to a natural notch. A tear is most often found in the lower segment, between the 5 and 7 o'clock positions on the clock face, and a complete tear reaches the base. A natural notch occurs in different segments of the hymen, mostly does not reach the base, and does not differ from other places. The state of the edges of a tear depends on its age: the edges of an old tear are thick and scarred.

t: Quick question: signs of sexual intercourse
n: Quick question: signs of sexual intercourse. Question: which signs confirm that sexual intercourse took place? Answer: finding semen in the vagina, development of pregnancy and transmission of sexually transmitted diseases. Semen usually persists in the vagina for up to 3–5 days, so the sooner the sample is taken, the more reliable the result. Remember: the sample for the laboratory should be taken as quickly as possible; over time reliability decreases.

Case analysis: virginity. Situation: there is doubt about the integrity of the hymen. The hymen may also be violated by a finger, objects or an operation. A tear bleeds for several days and scars by the end of the 2nd week to the 3rd week. After three weeks the age cannot be determined. Question: when and to whom does one turn? Answer: as soon as possible to a forensic medical expert, not to an obstetrician-gynaecologist.

Determination of reproductive capacity. In a man, reproductive capacity depends on intercourse and fertilisation, and in a woman on intercourse, conception and childbirth. In a man, impotence, azoospermia and necrospermia may be an obstacle. Impotence may arise from the central nervous system, endocrine diseases, defects of the genital organs or neurosis. Fertilising capacity is determined by laboratory examination of the ejaculate. In a woman, vaginal atresia, vaginismus, a narrow pelvis, scars and tumours are obstacles. Age, disease, defect, tumour and operations hinder the onset of pregnancy.

Signs of ongoing pregnancy. In pregnancy menstruation stops, but sometimes bloody discharge may occur. The breast and the areola enlarge and become pigmented; from the 2nd month this is clearly noticeable. The chorionic gonadotropin test and the change in uterine size are also among the signs. The reliable signs relate to the fetus: if the fetal heartbeat, body parts and movements are detected, pregnancy is reliably confirmed.

Signs of previous childbirth. In the first days the breasts are swollen, the areola is darker, and secretion is discharged. Cytological examination of the breast secretion helps determine the interval. The perineum is wide, the vaginal entrance is open, and the labia are swollen. In place of the hymen, myrtiform papillae with haemorrhages are found. The cervix is at first smooth and the external os is open; later it firms up. In a woman who has given birth the os is slit-like, in one who has not it is usually round. In a later period the interval is hard to determine, and one can only say that childbirth took place: slit-like os, myrtiform papillae, small scars on the abdominal skin.

Abortion, its types and criminal abortion. Abortion is termination of pregnancy up to the 22nd week. It may be spontaneous or artificial. In spontaneous abortion the cause is disease or poisoning. Medical abortion is carried out by an obstetrician-gynaecologist in a medical institution: 12 weeks at request, then on indication. Criminal abortion falls under Article 114 of the Criminal Code and is carried out by persons without training. It is performed by mechanical, chemical, sometimes thermal means, and very rarely with electric current. Complications: air embolism, traumatic shock, acute bleeding, perforation, poisoning, infection.

Case analysis: pregnancy and abortion. Situation: criminal abortion is suspected in a woman. The examination is carried out with the participation of an obstetrician-gynaecologist, with clinical-laboratory and instrumental examinations. The expert determines whether pregnancy and its termination occurred, by what method the termination was carried out, and what the consequences are. With the mechanical method, abrasions, bruises and wounds are found in the vagina and uterus. With the chemical method there are traces of poisoning and chemical burn. Question: traces of thermal burn and acute bleeding were found in the woman. Which method and which dangerous complications will you think of?

General classification of sexual offences. Rape is sexual intercourse using violence, threat, or taking advantage of a helpless state; it is given in Article 118 and is a crime against sexual freedom. Sodomy is sexual intercourse of a man with a man without violence, indicated in Article 120; if there is violence, Article 119 applies. Indecent acts are obscene, sensual acts against persons under 16; they are given in Article 129 and belong to the group of crimes against the family, youth and morals. Spreading a sexually transmitted disease or HIV falls under Article 113, a crime dangerous to life or health.

Rape, examination of the victim. Under Article 118, rape is sexual intercourse against the victim's will using violence, threat, or taking advantage of her helplessness. Theoretically men may also be victims, but in practice this crime is observed mainly against women. Before the examination, the decision ordering the examination, the record of the scene and the medical documents are studied; the interview and the gynaecological history are collected, that is menstruation, intercourse, childbirth, abortions. Rape is a legal concept: the expert looks for objective signs confirming intercourse or an attempt, violence and helplessness. Remember: a threat leaves no traces.

Injuries and samples in rape. In violence, bruises and abrasions are usually inflicted by the offender's hands and feet; they are found on the inner surface of the thighs, on the genitalia and on the neck. There may be a tear of the hymen, and sometimes tears of the vaginal wall and perineum are also observed. Injuries of the vagina and perineum may also occur in women who are sexually active. Semen is sought inside the vagina and on the pubis, perineum and thigh: a smear is taken from the vagina, and imprints from the pubis, perineum and thigh. The sample is taken as quickly as possible after the event, because over time the chance of finding spermatozoa decreases.

t: States of helplessness and traces of injury
n: States of helplessness and traces of injury. Helplessness may be associated with mental illness, trauma, physical defects, or young or old age. It may also be associated with alcohol or narcotic intoxication, or the action of stupefying substances. In violence, bruises and abrasions are inflicted by the offender's hands and feet; sometimes there are bite marks on the breast and neck. In a struggle or self-defence, bruises, abrasions and other injuries may be observed on various parts of the body.

Unnatural method and sodomy. Attention: Article 119 is not equal to Article 120. In one there is violence, threat or helplessness, in the other consent without violence. Under Article 119, when committed with violence, threat or taking advantage of helplessness, only the active participant is liable. Article 120 concerns relations of a man with a man without violence, and both the active and the passive participant are liable. In the active participant, particles of blood, hair and faeces and an oily substance persist for a long time in the coronal sulcus of the penis. In the passive participant there are abrasions, haemorrhages and fissures; with few acts no changes may be found.

t: Suspects and examination of the unnatural method
n: Suspects and examination of the unnatural method. In the unnatural method, the oral cavity and surrounding area, the anus and surrounding area, and the lower part of the rectum are examined. From these areas smears and imprints are taken for laboratory examination. In rape it is advisable to subject suspects to examination as well: bruises, abrasions and bite marks may be found. If traces of blood belonging to the woman, and hair, are found on the penis and pubis, they are taken for laboratory examination. In sodomy, suspected persons are sent for forensic medical examination as soon as possible.

Risk of misinterpretation in sodomy. With few sexual acts, in an adult passive participant, no injury or change may be found in the anal region and rectum. Constipation, diarrhoea, proctitis, paraproctitis, haemorrhoids, rectal prolapse or traces of previous surgery may be misinterpreted. Therefore attention is paid to these conditions at the interview, and if necessary the advice of a specialist proctologist is obtained. Attention: if violence, threat or helplessness was used, only the active participant is liable under Article 119; the passive participant is the victim.

Indecent acts. These are obscene acts of a sensual nature directed at a person under sixteen. The aim is to satisfy one's own need or to arouse feeling in the child. Examples: touching the genitalia with the hand or penis, undressing in front of the child, showing pornographic images and films. In the Criminal Code they belong to the group of crimes against the family, youth and morals; liability is established by Article 129. There may be redness, abrasions, bruises, haemorrhage in the hymen or an incomplete tear; in some cases no traces remain.

t: Sexually transmitted diseases and the spread of HIV/AIDS
n: Sexually transmitted diseases and the spread of HIV and AIDS. HIV is the human immunodeficiency virus, and AIDS is acquired immune deficiency syndrome. A dermatovenerologist and an AIDS specialist take part in the examination; a person in a late stage is a subject of the offence. Infecting with HIV or AIDS through improper performance of official duties also entails liability; this applies to medical staff. Sexual offences and groups of articles: rape, Article 118; sodomy, Article 120; indecent acts, Article 129; spreading a sexually transmitted disease and HIV or AIDS, Article 113, a crime dangerous to life or health.

Case analysis: sexual offences. Situation: a woman was brought for examination on suspicion of rape. A short time has passed since the event; there may be bruises on the thighs and semen in the vagina. The expert first studies the decision, the record of the scene and the medical documents. Then he conducts the interview and collects the gynaecological history. A smear from the vagina and imprints from the pubis, perineum and thigh are taken as quickly as possible. The more time passes, the lower the chance of finding spermatozoa. Question: should the suspect also be examined, and what is sought in that case?

To help memorise, we review and look at the errors. Semen usually persists in the vagina for 3–5 days. The sooner the sample is taken, the more reliable the result. The age of a violation of hymenal integrity can be determined only in the first weeks; after three weeks this question cannot be resolved. Indecent acts mean committing obscene acts against persons under 16, which is Article 129. Attention: Article 119 is not equal to Article 120. Under Article 119 there is violence, and only the active participant is liable. Under Article 120 there is no violence, and both are liable.

Conclusion. Examination of sexual conditions is ordered to determine sex, sexual maturity, virginity, reproductive capacity, pregnancy, childbirth and abortion. Sexual offences include rape, sodomy and indecent acts. In them the expert looks for objective medical and biological signs. Risk of expert error: proctitis, haemorrhoids or traces of surgery may be wrongly interpreted as a sign of passive sodomy. Test yourself: 1) the stages of the examination algorithm; 2) the difference between Articles 118, 119 and 120; 3) why should the sample be taken quickly?
